name: NJ-10
label: Safe D

key_factors: Incumbency in a safe Democratic seat
model.rationale: NJ-10's D+27 lean, McIver's massive financial advantage, and markets pricing her at 99% all point to a safe Democratic hold; the baseline margin of 28 points fits the fundamentals with no contrary evidence.
model.watch: A surprise scandal or legal development involving McIver could tighten the race, though the district's lean makes an upset very unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
LaMonica McIver, the Democratic incumbent, is heavily favored to win a second full term in this Newark-based district. The seat carries a D+27 partisan lean, and McIver has raised over $2.1 million against roughly $2,000 for Republican Carmen Bucco, who reports about $1,000 on hand. No outside groups are spending against her, and prediction markets put her chances at 99 percent.

No public general-election polls or expert ratings are available for this race, so the forecast rests on district fundamentals, the money gap, and market pricing. With such a lopsided resource and structural advantage, the race is rated Safe Democratic, with the main uncertainty being the exact size of the margin rather than the winner.
